title: The complex numbers are constructible in this kernel at zero trusted declarations, as a pair setoid over the constructed reals
statement: Let Complex be the one-constructor inductive with two CReal fields -- CReal being the Bishop setoid of regular rational sequences, itself constructed and axiom-free -- and let Complex.Equiv z w be the DEFINED relation CReal.Equiv (re z) (re w) AND CReal.Equiv (im z) (im w). Then the nine equality-only laws of the Real package -- add_comm, add_assoc, add_zero, add_neg, mul_comm, mul_assoc, mul_one, mul_zero, left_distrib -- all hold over Complex in Equiv form, each by a theorem whose axiom footprint is empty, and the whole environment carrying them has a trusted surface (Axiom + Opaque + Quotient) of zero. No quotient is taken at either level, so Quot.sound is not needed; no funext and no propext are needed either. Eq Complex is NOT the equality of complex numbers; Complex.Equiv is, and every law that mentions equality says so in its own statement.

formal.statement: Complex : Type, Complex.mk : CReal -> CReal -> Complex, Complex.Equiv : Complex -> Complex -> Prop := fun z w => And (CReal.Equiv (Complex.re z) (Complex.re w)) (CReal.Equiv (Complex.im z) (Complex.im w)); and for each L in {add_comm, add_assoc, add_zero, add_neg, mul_comm, mul_assoc, mul_one, mul_zero, left_distrib}, Complex.L is a checked Theorem with Kernel::axiom_footprint = [].

evidence.supports: Associativity of complex multiplication -- the law whose two sides are the same eight monomials in different orders, and the one that pays for the ring calculus on its own -- is a checked theorem with an empty axiom footprint.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example complex_ring_witness 2>/dev/null) && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE '^law[[:space:]]+Complex[.]mul_assoc[[:space:]]+\[\]$'
evidence.notes: Anchored on the law name AND the empty-footprint column, so a rename or a witness that grew a dependency on a trusted declaration both fail. The `law` rows go to stdout; the summary goes to stderr, which is why this row and the population row below capture different streams.

evidence.supports: Distributivity -- the law that ties the additive and multiplicative structures together, so the pair of rows cannot both pass on additive-only work.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example complex_ring_witness 2>/dev/null) && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE '^law[[:space:]]+Complex[.]left_distrib[[:space:]]+\[\]$'
evidence.notes: Second law, from the interaction of the two operations rather than from either alone.

evidence.supports: All nine laws hold, every named declaration is checked with an empty footprint, the whole environment's trusted surface is zero, and the carrier is inhabited and Equiv-discriminating on BOTH components -- the example exits non-zero otherwise.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example complex_ring_witness 2>&1) && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE '9/9 ring laws have an EMPTY axiom footprint'
evidence.notes: Captures BOTH streams: the per-declaration and per-law rows go to stdout and the summary to stderr, so the obvious `2>/dev/null` form silently matches nothing and passes for the wrong reason -- the same trap the creal population row records. The nine come from ComplexPrelude::ring_laws read out of the kernel, so dropping or duplicating a law flips the exit status instead of shrinking a count.
evidence.verified_negative: Removing the `neg` from Complex.mul's real part (making it a-c + b-e) makes the build fail and this command exit non-zero; removing the normalizer's cancellation pass does the same via add_neg and mul_conj.

evidence.supports: The environment carrying Complex, CReal, Rat, Int and Nat together has a trusted surface of zero -- Axiom AND Opaque AND Quotient, not Axiom alone.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example complex_ring_witness 2>&1) && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE 'trusted surface = 0 \(empty\)'
evidence.notes: Opaque has no proof body and Quotient admits Quot.sound, so an Axiom-only count can read zero while trusted declarations are present. This anchors on the count the example computes over all three kinds.

provenance.source: hand-built as a pair carrier over the CReal setoid of ADR-0483

notes: WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It does not claim a FIELD: there is no inverse, no division, no square root, no completeness and no algebraic closure, and none of those is one of the nine. It does not claim an order -- see F:complex-admits-no-compatible-order, which refutes one. It does not retire any Real axiom: the Real package is an ORDERED ring and Complex is not a model of it, only of its equality-only fragment. And Eq Complex is not on offer as equality of complex numbers; Complex.Equiv is.
